chapter: Later bands, Joe Turner and records
title: Kidrick Johnson's big band
summary: Fifteen years in the band, personnel and Reed Coleman.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Who was Kidrick Johnson?
That's Kidrick Johnson. That's who I got this letter here from his grandmother. Oh, I see. He's a local musician, saxophone player. Yeah.
Oh, I saw in a magazine, you know, David Griffith had a...
Yeah, well, I've had...I've worked with him about 15 years.
Yeah. Kidrick.
Yeah, I worked with him 15 years.
I just never did...was it a big band or a small band?
Big band.
Do you know any of the guys then? Do you remember them now?
In Kidrick's band?
Mm-hmm.
Well, he had Nat Doll.
Mm-hmm.
Oh, in this recent years, he had Teddy Riley. Mm-hmm. Teddy Riley just come out of that band when he went down there.
Down under the crazy chair, like some...
Yeah, he was writing, he was writing the music, arranging for us. Mm-hmm. And he had the two Knox brothers on saxophone. And Harley Thompson. Mm-hmm.
On saxophone.

Yeah. And he had me on guitar. Mm-hmm. Miss Olivia Charlotte on piano. And Joe Simon on bass. David Bickham on drum. Mm-hmm. That was the band. But for half of those 15 years my son played drums with us. And we had a drum bass player by the name of Reed Coleman. Oh, I see. Yeah. You ever heard of him? Heard of him? He left here and went to New York to live. Oh, is he playing music up there or just... I don't know what Reed Coleman doing.
I don't know what anybody would move to New York for in there. I don't know.

He had a better job off the time. Oh, yeah. He was a school teacher here. Oh, I see. And then he was a college man. He had a big degree, you know. He had opportunities. And so I guess he had something better off him. Because he left... He had built a home out in Gentilly and he left him. He rented that house out and moved to New York.
